newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE March sugar ends higher, other whites ease - Jan 23.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE March sugar ends higher, other whites ease - Jan 23.

text.p: London white sugar futures ended Thursday's session mostly weaker on trade selling but the spot March contract managed to retain some of the day's gains.

Traders said continued fund short selling in New York put a dampener on London's prospects, although these were already capped by overhead supply and a downtrend that has formed on March since the beginning of the year.
March whites finished the day 80 cents higher at $295.50 a tonne after reaching a session high of $297.00 led by trade and commission house buying. Its lowest level for the day was $294.60.
Turnover was an impressive 4,161 lots but traders noted a substantial volume of crosses and against actuals.
At the close May surrendered its premium to March while August was 70 cents ahead.
The market derived little support from a nine-day strike at the Colombian port of Buenaventura which paralysed at least 27,000 tonnes of bagged and bulk sugar.
The news, helped by the possibility of further export cuts, has driven coffee contracts to a sequence of highs in the past week.
